newsitem.title: USA: CBOT December corn limit down, soy falls on rains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT December corn limit down, soy falls on rains.

text.p: CBOT September and December corn futures fell the 12-cent per bushel daily limit in opening trade and soybeans were sharply lower after rains fell in parched portions of Illinois, traders said.
More rains were expected on Monday and Tuesday, easing concerns of heat and moisture stress, the traders said.

Meteorologists said rains had reached about 50 percent of central Illinois by early Monday with rainfall amounts ranging from 0.25 to 1.00 inch. Forecasts called for roughly 0.50 to 1.50 inches through Tuesday with 60 to 80 percent coverage.
Recent rains had bypassed central Illinois, leaving some fields in dire need of moisture.
At 0934 CDT, corn was down seven to 11 cents per bushel with December down 11 at $2.43. Soybeans were down 18-1/4 to 24-1/2 cents per bushel with November down 20-1/2 at $5.87.
